extracted.intended_audience: ALSC / John Newbery Medal committee chairs, committee members, ALSC staff, and prospective award committee appointees
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, behavioral standards, confidentiality rules, and administrative responsibilities for members and chairs of the ALSC John Newbery Medal selection committee, including balloting rules, re-balloting, Honor Book selection, and staff/PGC roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book discussion conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for how committee members should conduct themselves during book discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: speak loudly enough to be heard by everyone; refer back to the criteria to keep the discussion focused; be concise and avoid repeating what others have said; speak to the group as a whole; listen openly to other committee members and respond thoughtfully; be courteous and refrain from relating personal anecdotes; make comparisons only in relationship to other eligible books (do not compare a book with an author’s body of work or with books published before the year under consideration); focus first on a book’s strengths before its weaknesses; be as even-handed as possible (books do not always require the same length of discussion); conclude with a closing statement from the committee member who introduced the book (this practice provides for balance: the negative and the positive). For further reading, see Thom Barthelmess’s and Vicky Smith’s articles on book discussion guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balloting procedure and point scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal method for casting and tabulating selection ballots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members list first, second, and third place votes in an online tool. In tabulating ballots the tool assigns four points to each first-place vote, three points to each second-place vote, and two points to each third-place vote. The online tool uses a specific formula to determine the winner (see Winner threshold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Winner threshold and Chair voting recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical threshold and margin required for a book to win the Medal/Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book must receive at least eight first-choice votes at four points each for a total of at least thirty-two points, and it must have an eight-point lead over the book receiving the next highest number of points. If the committee is operating an odd number of members down, it is recommended that the Chair refrain from voting, as an even number of committee members makes it significantly harder for a book to achieve the margin of points needed to win. If a committee is operating an even number of members down, the Awards Coordinator can adjust the formula used in the online balloting tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-balloting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and constraints for re-opening discussion and conducting additional ballots when no winner is produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee may not proceed to another ballot without a second round of book discussion. By consensus the committee may choose to withdraw from the discussion list all books that received no votes on the first ballot and may withdraw additional books that received minimal support. Once withdrawn from the discussion list, a book is permanently eliminated from consideration. After second-round discussion a second ballot is held using the same point system and formula. If after a second ballot there is still no winner, the committee is required to re-open discussion and then re-ballot, alternating between discussion and re-balloting until a winner is selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor Books selection policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for choosing Honor Books after a winner is selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no requirement that Honor Books be named and no rule dictating the number. There is an expectation that Honor Books be truly distinguished, not merely strong contenders. The committee considers whether to select Honor Books; options include using the winning selection ballot to choose Honor Books (looking at titles with the next highest number of points) or holding one additional ballot (only one additional ballot allowed). The Honor Book selection ballot consists of titles from the winning selection ballot that received points (the winner is eliminated); by consensus, titles with no remaining support may also be withdrawn. Honor Books are announced to the public in alphabetical order by title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on secrecy and non-disclosure before, during, and after the selection to protect the integrity of deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members must maintain secrecy regarding the selection outcome prior to the ALA YMA Press Conference. Publishing house employees and winners must also maintain secrecy prior to the press conference. Confidentiality is intended to protect the privacy of committee members, allow frank closed-meeting discussion, and preserve the element of surprise. The details of the Selection Meeting should never be disclosed. The following items are explicitly not for public discussion at any time prior to, during, or following the selection: (1) Reasons (other than your own) given by individual committee members for nominating, supporting, or removing a book from consideration (the committee’s reasons will be given by the Chair or a designate); (2) Specific titles or lists of titles under consideration; (3) The number of ballots necessary for any decision or the vote in any balloting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting and handling the press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Chair's responsibility for preparing the committee's public justification and working with ALA CMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After selection the Chair prepares a draft press release (usually with assistance from committee members), using background information about the winners and justification statements about the winning books. The Chair is responsible for delivering the draft press release, copies of the Medal/Award and Honor Books, and any other requested information to the ALA Communications & Marketing Office (CMO) by the designated deadline and in the designated format. The CMO finalizes the press release to be distributed immediately after the ALA YMA Press Conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award and Honor Book notification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: How winners are contacted and timing of notification prior to public announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee Chair will receive information concerning timing and method of communication with the award winners from the CMO and the Awards Coordinator prior to LibLearnX and will inform all committee members. ALSC staff contact publishers and winners after the Chair provides required contact information; communications are coordinated to preserve confidentiality until the official announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press conference logistics and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational expectations for committee presence and behavior at the ALA YMA Press Conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee reconvenes at the CMO headquarters on the morning of the ALA YMA Press Conference; committee members are usually asked to pose for a group photograph and should be present a few minutes before the scheduled time. It is imperative the press conference start on time. At the conference the President announces the winner and Honor books and committee members are asked to stand for recognition when their award is announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations guidance after selection
rubrics_metrics.description: How committee members should interact with local and national media after selections are public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members may work with local news media to publicize ALSC awards; if interviewed, emphasize the role librarians play in selecting titles, the value of making distinguished books accessible, the award criteria, and the committee’s reasons for its choices as stated in the press release. If contacted by national media, committee members should immediately email details to the Chair, PGC, ALSC Executive Director and the current ALSC President and await further instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence and transition documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Chair responsibilities for correspondence, appreciation, and transferring useful information to successor Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair sends appreciation letters to members and members’ employers. Chair sends the next Chair a list of any potentially eligible books with next year’s copyright date that the committee identified, plus friendly suggestions about procedural matters. Note: Providing a committee’s entire discussion list would violate confidentiality. The Chair also submits a final Quarterly Report along with meeting minutes to appropriate ALSC leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and archival of committee materials
rubrics_metrics.description: What materials ALSC archives and when they may be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALSC preserves suggestion lists, nomination lists, and justification statements (with names redacted); minutes (kept so they do not include confidential discussion points); the Chair’s press remarks; copies of congratulatory letters; and the Chair’s award presentation remarks, adding these materials to the current archive. ALSC permits publication of this information after a period of 50 years following the presentation of the medal/award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair's role in discussion leadership and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral expectations for the Chair balancing facilitation duties with voting membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chair is a voting member with the same rights and responsibilities and must balance being Chair and committee member. Many Chairs find it helpful to limit remarks to books they feel strongly about, speak later in the discussion, and speak only to make a novel point. The Chair must be ready to abstain from voting if the committee is balloting one member down. The Chair sets the tone for committee discussion by accepting relevant statements, leading discussion on pertinent issues, ensuring all members are allowed to speak, and preventing any one member from dominating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair administrative and operational duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific administrative tasks the Chair must perform throughout the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: attend Chair orientation (usually online); place calls for book recommendations across ALSC outlets; check eligibility of suggested/nominated books with assistance from the PGC; answer correspondence promptly and copy committee members, Awards Coordinator, and PGC; submit budget requests and maintain financial records; request reimbursements as applicable; prepare and submit Quarterly Reports electronically; contact non-participating members and, if necessary after consultation with PGC, suggest resignation; represent the committee at Division Leadership meetings and PGC meetings; attend ALA YMA Press Conference briefing; present problems to the PGC and Awards Coordinator as needed; prepare remarks for award presentation as directed by ALSC office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative assistant role and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for appointing and using a non-voting administrative assistant to support the Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chair may request an administrative assistant, a volunteer who helps with administrative tasks. Although not a voting member, the Administrative Assistant is held to the same standards of confidentiality as other committee members. The Administrative Assistant is not required to attend conferences, although virtual participation may be requested to facilitate committee deliberations. The Chair should direct requests for an assistant to the Awards Coordinator, the Program Officer for Governance, and the President at the time of their appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of ALSC membership in suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: How ALSC members-at-large may suggest books and how those suggestions are handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chair is responsible for calling for books to consider several times during the year via the ALSC blog, website, ALA Connect, social media, Children and Libraries journal, and other lists. Suggestions from members-at-large are collated using an online tool; books submitted by members-at-large are accepted up to two weeks before the LibLearnX Selection Meeting. The committee is not obligated to include books submitted by members-at-large on the LibLearnX discussion list, but members should take suggestions seriously. At LibLearnX only books nominated by committee members are considered, along with further suggestions moved forward after nominations are complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Group Consultant (PGC) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Role and duties of the assigned PGC for the award committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PGC is assigned to address questions from the Chair and committee regarding procedure, personnel, and book eligibility (this position is PGC V - Awards). The PGC works with the Chair to annually review committee procedures and make recommendations for improvement (ranging from easy implementations to those requiring Board action). Committee members consult the PGC for unusual issues the Chair cannot resolve, particularly issues regarding the Chair. The PGC may attend the Introductory Meeting and/or Initial Discussion Meeting to explain their role to the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALSC staff support responsibilities (general and meeting-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: What ALSC staff provide to ensure committee operations and meeting logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALSC staff tasks include: checking eligibility for membership; sending formal invitations; providing the Chair with an electronic contacts form and publishing roster once forms are completed; assisting with calls for ALSC membership suggestions; creating online forms for suggestions/nominations/membership suggestions; requesting secured rooms for meetings and communicating access details. At LibLearnX staff create online balloting forms and provide links to the Chair, provide Chair with contact information for winners, provide access to forms for listing winners and official comments, and work with ALA CMO on announcement logistics. After LibLearnX staff send letters of congratulations to winners and publishers, work with winners/publishers on acceptance speeches and presentation logistics, arrange engraving and awards preparation, provide copies of previous presentation speeches, and continue aiding CMO in publicizing awards. At the celebration staff bring medals/awards and handle last-minute presentation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALSC President responsibilities for committee appointments and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties of the ALSC President related to award committee membership and ceremonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President appoints members and the Chair, fills committee vacancies if necessary, deals with conflicts of interest or non-participation in consultation with the Executive Committee and the PGC, and presides at announcement and presentation ceremonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility, disclosure, and conflict-of-interest checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and disclosures prospective committee members must complete and consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective members must answer a checklist (yes/no) about service elsewhere in ALA, contracts for children's trade books to be published during service, recent employment/consulting for publishers/authors/illustrators, close relatives who are authors/illustrators or employed by U.S. trade publishers, direct ownership of >5% equity in a U.S. trade publishing company, personal relationships that could cause perceived conflicts, anticipated difficulty attending required meetings, difficulty accessing newly published children's books, prior service on certain committees in the past four years. A 'yes' does not necessarily preclude service but should be discussed with the Executive Director before accepting appointment; failure to disclose may lead to immediate dismissal. Prospective members must verify they have read and understand the social media/service guideline (including ceasing signed reviews from the start of term). They must provide social media usernames and review outlet information where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on public discussion, signed reviews and social media for eligible titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on members' public communications about eligible titles during their term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should not use social media or electronic forms of communication in relation to eligible titles during their term of service, except for virtual committee work in closed forums (email, private ALA Connect groups, Zoom). Prohibited forms include Facebook, Twitter, Goodreads, LibraryThing, blogs, and review websites. Award committee members may not publish bylined (signed) reviews that feature titles eligible for their award during their term because committee affiliation is public and published reviews could be used to question impartiality. Exceptions and permissible activities include: members may write and publish unsigned reviews of any book; members of all committees (except Batchelder) may write signed reviews or discuss via social media any book previously published in other countries or by an author/illustrator who is not an American citizen or resident; Batchelder committee members may write signed reviews or discuss via social media any book that has not been translated and published in the U.S. in the previous year; committee-specific guidance (e.g., Caldecott, Newbery, Belpré, Sibert, Geisel) gives members other permissible review/discussion domains. At no time during or after service may committee members discuss the status of books as having been or not having been a consideration, suggested, and/or nominated for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of when members must cease/write reviews (term start and resumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the prohibition on signed reviews/social media begins and when members may resume reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALSC policy indicates members may not engage in print or electronic communication regarding eligible titles during their 'term of service,' which officially begins July 1 of the appointment year (or immediately upon appointment after that date). Once the committee’s selections have been announced at the LibLearnX Youth Media Awards Press Conference, members may then write bylined reviews, articles, and blog posts even though the term does not end until the following Annual Conference. Note: prohibition includes galleys produced after July 1 because publication dates can be delayed making a book eligible; thus the July 1 cutoff is used to be safe and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on writing teachers’ or readers’ guides for trade publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Members cannot serve in advisory capacities to trade publishers by writing guides during service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy does not permit committee members to write teachers’ guides or readers’ group guides for children’s trade-book publishers during their term of service because this falls under serving in an advisory capacity to a trade publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on minor reference assistance and acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification that ordinary reference assistance does not constitute disqualifying advisory service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assistance as part of ordinary library reference duties (e.g., helping an author with research questions) does not disqualify a member from serving on an award committee, even if the author acknowledges the librarian in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedication of a book to a committee member
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to resign if an eligible book is dedicated to a member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a children’s book is dedicated to a member and will come out during the member’s term of service (and is eligible for consideration), the member may not accept appointment; if the member learns of the dedication once term begins, they are expected to resign as soon as they find out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal friendships with authors/illustrators
rubrics_metrics.description: How personal relationships affect eligibility to serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having a friend who is a children’s book author does not automatically bar service; it might if the friend is a close personal friend who publishes an eligible book every year. If the friend does not have an eligible book during the year of service, there's no issue.
